items.title: Self-loot, currency and roll-won patterns rebuild when the chat globals they were compiled from change (PrettyChat rewrites them mid-session)
items.spec: core/Util.lua: Util.BuildLootPatterns, Util.BuildCurrencyPatterns and Util.RollWonPattern record the exact source global strings they compiled from (a parallel array or a joined key of LOOT_ITEM_SELF_MULTIPLE ... LOOT_ITEM_REFUND, CURRENCY_GAINED_* , LOOT_ROLL_YOU_WON). Util.ParseSelfLoot, Util.ParseSelfCurrency and Util.ParseRollWon compare the current globals against the recorded sources on each parse (cheap rawequal string compares, no allocation on the hit path) and rebuild on any difference, including a global that appeared or disappeared (rollWonPattern's cached false must not survive LOOT_ROLL_YOU_WON appearing). Keep the parse hot path allocation-free when nothing changed (performance rules for CHAT_MSG_LOOT). Update the comments that say 'compiled once' to say 'compiled once per distinct set of globals' and name the reason (another addon such as PrettyChat rewrites these globals at runtime; PrettyChat docs call it handoff H-1). No PrettyChat change and no bus message. No GitHub issue is opened (OWNER_SCOPE 5: no issue writes beyond named issues). tests/test_util.lua gains cases: 'a rewritten LOOT_ITEM_SELF is honoured on the next parse without a reload', 'a rewritten CURRENCY_GAINED_MULTIPLE is honoured', 'LOOT_ROLL_YOU_WON appearing after a nil first parse is honoured', and 'an unchanged global set does not rebuild' (count Build calls). Each written red first.
items.steps:
1. Write the four test_util cases; run, confirm red (stale patterns).
2. Implement source tracking + rebuild-on-change in core/Util.lua.
3. Green gate; check no per-parse table allocation (tests/perf.lua scenario for loot lines unchanged within noise).
4. Regenerate docs/test-cases.md (`lua tests/run.lua --list > docs/test-cases.md`) and move the README Tests badge to the new Totals pass count in the same commit.
5. Commit `LH-01: ...`.

items.title: Util.Coalesce: a window canceled by the stand-down no longer wedges the trigger for the rest of the session
items.spec: core/Util.lua Util.Coalesce (around :249-268): replace the `pending` boolean with the NS.After handle (or a generation counter) so a window canceled by NS.StandDown (core/LifecycleSetup.lua) is treated as not pending; the next trigger after stand-up arms a fresh window.
